Article Title: Centre tells SC it is open to tougher labels on packaged foods high in sugar, salt or fat
Article Text:
Supreme Court Justice JB Pardiwala questioned why the FSSAI was taking a two-phased approach.

NIN flags gaps in proposed system

Why the labels matter

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Thursday told the Supreme Court that it was willing to consider stronger warning labels on packaged food, opening the door to tighter front-of-pack labelling rules that could have a significant impact on the country's packaged food industry.The issue concerns a proposed system under which food packets would carry prominent red hexagonal warnings to alert consumers when products contain high levels of nutrients linked to health risks, reported news agency Reuters.The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) had recently proposed introducing the labelling system in two phases. Under the initial plan, a product would get a red warning symbol if it crossed the prescribed limits in at least two of three categories, namely added sugar, salt or saturated fat. Tighter provisions were to follow in the second phase.Health experts and activists have opposed this approach, arguing that requiring a product to be high in two nutrients before triggering a warning could allow several unhealthy products to avoid the label.The Supreme Court questioned the need for such a phased approach during Thursday's hearing."It has to be sugar ‌and salt. Only then will you ask them to put a label?" Justice JB Pardiwala asked the government's lawyer, stressing the word "and".Additional Solicitor General Brijender Chahar, appearing for FSSAI, said the regulator could now consider implementing both phases together following the court's observation.That could mean a product would carry a red warning if it crosses the limit for even one of the specified nutrients, whether added sugar, salt or saturated fat.The matter has been under the Supreme Court's consideration for months following petitions seeking stronger front-of-pack nutrition warnings. The court had recently given FSSAI a two-week deadline to come back with its proposals.As that deadline approached, the National Institute of Nutrition in Hyderabad submitted its suggestions to the food regulator.NIN has argued that the proposed system should not focus only on added sugar and added fat. It has suggested that factors such as total calories, total sugar and total fat should also be taken into account when deciding whether a packaged food needs a warning.The concern is that looking at only selected nutrients could allow some foods with an unhealthy overall nutritional profile to escape the warning system.A scientist from NIN explained this using fried snacks as an example. A packet of salty fried chips may contain little added sugar and could fall below the proposed threshold for added fat, while still being extremely calorie-dense because of its fat content.Under a system focused only on added sugar and added fat, such a product could therefore avoid a red warning despite being unhealthy when consumed frequently.Front-of-pack nutrition labelling is intended to give consumers an easy-to-understand warning without requiring them to study detailed nutritional information printed on the back of a packet.The proposed red hexagon is designed to work much like a stop sign, with words such as "high fat", "high sugar" or "high salt" clearly displayed depending on which limit a product crosses.NIN has also pointed out that the nutritional quality of a food cannot necessarily be determined simply by whether it is ultra-processed. A samosa or jalebi, for instance, may be high in fat or sugar without being classified as an ultra-processed food. At the same time, some whole-grain breakfast cereals may be ultra-processed but relatively low in fat, salt and sugar.The debate before the court is therefore not merely about the shape or colour of a label. It is about what nutritional criteria should trigger a warning and whether the proposed system is strong enough to help consumers identify foods that could be harmful when eaten regularly.
Article Summary: Centre willing to consider stronger warning labels on packaged food. Issue concerns a proposed system under which food packets would carry prominent red hexagonal warnings. Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) had proposed introducing the labelling system in two phases. Under the initial plan, a product would get a red warning symbol if it crossed the prescribed limits in at least two of three categories.

Article Title: AI making it difficult for central banks to determine growth potential: BIS
Article Text:
AI is making it harder for central banks to determine an economy’s potential growth rate.

Mumbai:

AI is making it harder for central banks to determine an economy’s potential growth rate, as technological change increases uncertainty around productivity, potential output and the natural rate of interest, BIS general manager Pablo Hernández de Cos said.“AI is reshaping demand, supply and financial markets simultaneously, making the economy harder to read and increasing uncertainty around the transmission of monetary policy,” Hernández de Cos said at the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai on Thursday.While the objectives of monetary policy remain unchanged, AI-driven structural changes could make some of the key variables that guide policy harder to estimate, he said. Potential output and the natural rate of interest are already subject to significant uncertainty, and rapid changes driven by AI could widen measurement errors and increase discrepancies between actual and estimated output gaps.The longer-term economic impact of AI is also uncertain, Hernández de Cos said, pointing to three scenarios outlined in the BIS Annual Economic Report. In one, AI produces a bounded productivity boost that permanently raises the growth trend.In another, AI generates self-reinforcing, transformative growth as the technology improves itself. A third scenario, the “demand bottleneck”, sees automation diverting income from labour towards further AI investment, eventually weakening consumer spending and causing productivity and output growth to stall.These scenarios could have very different implications for the natural rate of interest and inflation, he said. Stronger productivity growth could raise r-star, while a demand bottleneck could eventually push it below pre-AI levels and become disinflationary.“The takeaway from this analysis is that there is considerable uncertainty about the long-term effects of AI,” Hernández de Cos said. The eventual outcome would depend on how much AI progress relies on consumer demand, how competition affects profit margins in the AI sector and how quickly AI products and infrastructure depreciate.Hernández de Cos flagged financial-stability risks from the AI investment boom, with concentrated equity valuations, capex outpacing cash flows and rising reliance on debt/private credit. Opaque “circular financing” between chipmakers, hyperscalers and AI firms could amplify losses if AI returns disappoint, turning the investment boom into a bust.AI could also deliver major productivity gains, with studies showing 10-65% task-level gains and 20-50% time savings; median estimates suggest a 0.5 percentage-point annual boost to total factor productivity. But benefits will be uneven: AI may augment skilled work while displacing routine cognitive jobs, with informal workers in developing economies particularly vulnerable. Early displacement is emerging in customer support, programming and administration, making reskilling essential.Advanced economies are better placed to capture near-term gains, though preparedness varies sharply among emerging markets. India has an opportunity to close the gap by building on its digital public infrastructure. Rather than replicate full AI ecosystems, countries should target comparative advantages across chips, cloud, data, models and applications, including local-language models and domain-specific data.For central banks, AI raises the premium on measurement, judgement, policy agility and international cooperation. Its economic impact will ultimately depend on policy choices, including investment in digital infrastructure and skills, competition, data governance and sound institutions.
Article Summary: AI is making it harder for central banks to determine an economy’s potential growth rate. technological change increases uncertainty around productivity, potential output and the natural rate of interest, BIS general manager Pablo Hernández de Cos said.

Article Title: Brics summit: 3 Russian aircraft touch down at Noida airport ahead of Putin's meet with PM Modi
Article Text:
Russian President Vladimir Putin’s three-day India visit will focus on defence, energy and economic ties, Ukraine and West Asia, with talks with PM Modi and participation in the BRICS summit on the agenda. (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Three Russian transport aircraft touched down at Noida International Airport on Thursday as world leaders began arriving in India ahead of the 18th BRICS Summit. The aircraft arrivals come a day ahead of Russian President Vladimir Putin's expected visit to New Delhi for the summit.Putin is also likely to hold a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday, September 11, before the multilateral event scheduled to be held in New Delhi on September 12 and 13.Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov had earlier confirmed that the meeting between Putin and PM Modi was scheduled for Friday. Speaking to reporters during a virtual briefing from Moscow, Peskov said, "We're looking forward to the President and Prime Minister having another bilateral meeting during the visit. It is scheduled. It is scheduled for Friday, so first, like always, they will touch on the bilateral agenda. Trade and economic cooperation is a very wide scope."Peskov said Putin's India visit would provide an opportunity for the two sides to discuss bilateral relations and expand cooperation. He also expressed hope that India would successfully host the Brics summit."In a couple of days, President Putin will begin his India visit.You know that our two leaders, Indian and Russian leaders, are in a very close personal contact. They are very pragmatic in their relationship, and they are as sincere as to be able to discuss in a very open and constructive way the most sensitive issues of our agenda and our bilateral relations. Of course, it opens additional horizons for our cooperation," Peskov said.On the Brics summit, he said Russia was working to support greater cooperation among member countries across key areas."We have no doubt that the summit will be successful. Russia, we are doing our best to contribute to further development of BRICS cooperation in the three main pillars of our interaction. So, those are policy and security, economy and finance, and cultural and humanitarian contexts. So, we are supporting the idea of inviting new countries to join different formats within BRICS," he noted.India is hosting the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12 and 13, 2026. The summit is being held under the theme, “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”
Article Summary: Three Russian transport aircraft touched down at Noida International Airport on Thursday as world leaders began arriving in India. The aircraft arrivals come a day ahead of Russian President Vladimir Putin's expected visit to New Delhi for the summit. Putin is also likely to hold a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday.

Article Title: 'Govt cremated body forcibly': Gulzar Singh's family alleges last rites conducted without consent
Article Text:
'Administration cremated the body forcibly, without our consent,' says Gulzar Singh's son.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The family of Gulzar Singh, a Dalit labourer from Punjab’s Sangrur district who died by suicide after allegedly facing harassment, has accused the "government of forcibly cremating his body without their consent. "Gulzar’s son Lakhwinder Singh alleged that the family was not allowed to see his father’s face before the last rites and that they did not receive his clothes or other belongings.Speaking to ANI on Thursday, Lakhwinder said, "The govt cremated the body forcibly, without our consent. We should get justice. Cheema sahib should be jailed."He also alleged that the government had promised the family a job and other assistance but failed to provide them."The government forcibly carried out the last rites. They told us they would provide a job and other things, but we received nothing. I was in a state of depression. The police pressure was immense; it was the district police. Yes, it happened without our consent. Didn't even let me see his face. Don't even get his clothes. I demand justice," he added.Earlier on Thursday, National Commission for Scheduled Castes chairman Kishor Makwana met Gulzar’s family.Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old member of the Valmiki community from Dirba in Sangrur district, died on Monday night after allegedly consuming poison.His family alleged that he was harassed, intimidated and subjected to caste-based abuse after he questioned Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema about the drug menace during a public meeting in Toor Banjara village on September 6.A purported video of Gulzar’s final statement shows him raising concerns with Cheema about the availability of ‘chitta’ in the area and saying his own son was also addicted to drugs.According to his family, police and local panchayat members allegedly pressured him to apologise after the incident. They claimed that some people also subjected him to caste-based abuse and asked him to appear before the village panchayat.Gulzar consumed poison around noon on Monday and was taken to hospitals in Sangrur and Patiala before being shifted to DMC Hospital in Ludhiana, where he died later that night.Police registered an FIR against five residents of Toor Banjara — Baljeet Singh, Sukhdev Singh, Vicky Singh, Gona Singh and Baljinder Kaur — under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for abetment to suicide and provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.The accused include the village sarpanch and her husband, according to the allegations. The sarpanch’s husband has denied the charges, saying the allegations against the panchayat were baseless.Dirba SHO Gurvinder Singh said further action would be based on medical and investigative findings.The case also triggered a political row in Punjab, with the BJP and Congress demanding action against Cheema and an independent probe.BJP leader Amit Malviya alleged that Gulzar was pressured by local AAP-linked village leaders after questioning Cheema over the drug menace.“Raising the issue of Punjab’s drug menace should not cost a citizen his life. Gulzar Singh, a resident of Toor Banjara village in the Dirba constituency, reportedly questioned AAP Minister Harpal Singh Cheema during his visit about the unchecked sale of “chitta”, saying that his own son was battling addiction and had sold off the family’s belongings. What followed, was pressure and harassment by local AAP-linked village leaders, who demanded that Gulzar Singh apologise for questioning the minister. He refused," Malviya said."In a video recorded before consuming poison, Gulzar Singh held four people responsible for his plight, including Harpal Cheema and local village leaders. He later died despite treatment. This is deeply disturbing. A government that cannot tolerate questions on the drug menace and intimidates a citizen for raising them has a serious case to answer. Punjab deserves accountability, not intimidation," he added.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi also attacked the AAP government, demanding that chief minister Bhagwant Mann seek Cheema’s resignation and ensure an independent investigation."A dangerous pattern is emerging under Punjab's AAP government - if you question government's failures, the response will come in the form of threats and torture," Rahul said."Gulzar Singh ji, from the Dalit community, who had to watch his son fall victim to drugs, asked the Finance Minister just this much: why has the government failed so miserably in stopping the drug trade? For just this, he was tortured and humiliated so much, pressured so intensely to apologize, that he consumed poison," he said.The government's job is to answer to the people, not to "trample upon" those who ask questions, he added.The AAP has accused the opposition of “vulture politics” and of trying to politically exploit the family’s grief. AAP media in-charge Baltej Pannu said, “Wherever someone dies by suicide or wherever a dead body is found, they reach there and try to bake political bread over the funeral pyre.”
Article Summary: Gulzar Singh, a Dalit labourer from Sangrur district, died on Monday night after allegedly consuming poison. His family alleged that he was harassed, intimidated and subjected to caste-based abuse after he questioned Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema about the drug menace.

Article Title: 'They would kick us': Stalin takes on Vijay over 'jaw gesture', recalls Emergency-era prison days
Article Text:
His remarks came after Vijay launched a strong attack on the DMK in the assembly

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: DMK president MK Stalin on Thursday hit back at Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay over his recent remarks in the state assembly, accusing him of attempting to demean the party and its leaders while recalling his arrest and alleged custodial torture during the Emergency.Responding to Vijay’s criticism of the DMK, Stalin said the party’s history and its ideological struggle could not be changed by political attacks.“Thambi Vijay, what you said is true. It is not a lie. During the Emergency, opposing it, leader Kalaignar organized a huge gathering at the Marina beach and severely criticized the MISA Act,” Stalin said in a video message shared on X.His remarks came after Vijay launched a strong attack on the DMK in the assembly on Wednesday, accusing previous governments of corruption and referring to the Sarkaria Commission as well as Enforcement Directorate documents concerning alleged corruption during the 2021-26 regime.Stalin recalled that the Union government dismissed the DMK government on January 31, 1976, during the Emergency imposed by the Indira Gandhi government.“The very next second after dismissing the government, police came to the Gopalapuram house to arrest me under the MISA Act,” Stalin said, recounting how his father and former chief minister M Karunanidhi told police that his son was away campaigning and would return the next day.Stalin said that after he returned, Karunanidhi himself called the police and asked them to arrest him.Recalling his time in prison, Stalin alleged that he was subjected to severe physical abuse and was kept with other prisoners in a small room where leprosy patients had earlier been housed.“In prison, many atrocities happened to me. We were taken and locked up in a place where leprosy patients were kept. Ten people were locked inside a small room. Inside that same room, in a single pot, all of us had to urinate,” he said.Stalin alleged that police beat prisoners with lathis at night, kicked them with boots and that other inmates also assaulted them. He recalled the death of DMK leader and former MP Chitti Babu, whom he said died in jail following the beatings.“Due to their beating, my dear brother, Member of Parliament Chitti Babu, died inside the jail itself. Due to their beating, my jawbone was broken,” Stalin said.The DMK has condemned Vijay’s remarks and announced a statewide protest on September 12, accusing the chief minister of making “scurrilous remarks” against Stalin, Karunanidhi and other party leaders.Law minister R Nirmal Kumar, however, has disputed Stalin’s account, saying there was no official record to indicate that his detention during the Emergency was under MISA. The minister said Stalin was arrested following remarks concerning Indira Gandhi and her 20-point programme.Stalin also rejected Vijay’s allegations relating to the Sarkaria Commission and corruption charges against Karunanidhi, arguing that successive governments would have acted if the allegations had been established.Turning to Vijay’s conduct in the Assembly, Stalin urged him to maintain the dignity expected of a chief minister and focus on governance rather than political controversies.“The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly has dignity and respect. It is a place sculpted by many great leaders, great men. That responsibility is now with you,” Stalin said.
Article Summary: DMK president MK Stalin hit back at Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay over his recent remarks. He accused Vijay of attempting to demean the party and its leaders while recalling his arrest and alleged custodial torture during the Emergency. Vijay launched a strong attack on the DMK in the assembly on Wednesday.

CHENNAI: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam president and chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Thursday announced Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama as the candidates of the party-led Secular Social Justice alliance for the upcoming by-elections to Mathurantagam and Dharapuram Assembly constituencies. Article Title: SC rejects 1993 blast accused Abu Salem's plea for early release from life term
Article Text:
Salem was extradited from Portugal on November 11, 2005, after a prolonged legal battle.

The Supreme Court dismissed a plea by gangster Abu Salem on Thursday after he sought an early release from custody for having completed 25 years in jail.Salem, who is serving a sentence in connection with the 1993 Mumbai serial blasts, was extradited from Portugal on November 11, 2005, following a prolonged legal battle.The extradition agreement between India and Portugal stipulated that Salem could not be sentenced to death and that his prison term could not exceed 25 years.A bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta upheld Bombay High Court’s April ruling, which had rejected his plea for immediate release, terming it “premature” and “misconceived”.A detailed order is yet to be released.Earlier in Feb, the Supreme Court refused to entertain Salem’s plea, which claimed that he was in "illegal custody" for over 10 months as he had already undergone the 25-year sentence awarded to him in the March 12, 1993, Mumbai serial bomb blasts case.
Article Summary: Salem is serving a sentence in connection with the 1993 Mumbai serial blasts. He was extradited from Portugal on November 11, 2005, following a prolonged legal battle. The extradition agreement between India and Portugal stipulated that Salem could not be sentenced to death and that his prison term could not exceed 25 years.

Article Title: 'I didn't see any benefits': Congress's P Chidambaram questions 2026 Brics, draws BJP's flak
Article Text:
Chidambaram's remarks came as authorities in the capital intensified preparations for the Brics summit.

BJP hits back at Congress

Delhi steps up preparations

Officials inspect key routes

NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader and Rajya Sabha MP P Chidambaram has questioned what India has gained from recent Brics meetings, saying he has not seen any tangible benefits from the last two or three summits.With India set to host the Brics Summit 2026 in Delhi, Chidambaram said the country is part of several major international groupings but questioned whether they had delivered concrete gains for India.“I don't know how many Presidents and how many Prime Ministers are coming. I don't think the last two or three Brics summits have resulted in tangible benefits or tangible results,” Chidambaram told news agency ANI.“In fact, we are part of Brics, we are part of SCO, we are part of G20, and we are part of Quad. What benefits are we getting out of that? I can't see. In the last two or three summits, I didn't see any benefits. Earlier, the Brics Summits resulted in some tangible benefits,” he added.Reacting to Chidambaram's remarks, BJP leader Nalin Kohli said it was surprising that the Congress leader had raised such questions at a time when India was preparing to host an important international event that would bring together several heads of state and government."One is surprised to note the statement of Mr Chidambaram and the Congress Party, particularly at a time when India is hosting such an important event, the BRICS Summit, where many heads of state and heads of government will come, and there will be direct meetings also, one-on-one meetings between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and these leaders," Kohli said.Questioning the approach adopted by the Congress towards diplomacy, the BJP leader asked whether international engagement should be assessed merely in terms of immediate, transactional gains."Is diplomacy to be seen as a transaction like the Congress Party is projecting? What have I done for you? What will you do for me? Kind of an approach. What is the so-called tangible result?" he said.Kohli then questioned the Congress party's own diplomatic record from Independence until 2014."If we talk of tangible results, we can question what the Congress Party's entire approach from 1947 right up to 2014 was on diplomacy, including Sharm El Sheikh and peer projecting Pakistan as literally a victim of terror when it is the perpetrator of terror," he stated.Chidambaram's remarks came as authorities in the capital intensified preparations for the summit. Delhi Municipal Corporation Commissioner Sanjeev Khirwar and PWD Principal Secretary Sandeep Kumar inspected key areas on Wednesday, including the summit venue and locations around Bharat Mandapam.Senior officials from both departments, including deputy commissioners from the concerned zones, accompanied them during the inspection.Khirwar reviewed sanitation and civic arrangements and directed officials to coordinate closely on cleanliness and other essential services.Officials were asked to carry out intensive cleaning and maintenance along summit routes, venues, adjoining areas, markets, roads, footpaths, green belts and other sensitive locations.The inspection also covered movement corridors in southeast Delhi, including Sarai Kale Khan, Lodhi Road and Nizamuddin, as well as Saket and Sheikh Sarai in south Delhi.Authorities were directed to deploy sufficient sanitation workers, machinery and supervisory staff during the final stage of preparations.Khirwar also called for visible improvements in enforcement, animal control, vector control, beautification, lighting and branding at identified locations.India is taking over the Brics chairship for the fourth time in 2026. The chairship is being guided by the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, with a stated focus on a people-centric and humanity-first approach.
Article Summary: Senior Congress leader and Rajya Sabha MP P Chidambaram has questioned what India has gained from recent Brics meetings. He said he has not seen any tangible benefits from the last two or three summits. India is set to host the Brics Summit 2026 in Delhi.

Article Title: 'Wonder if I should become a cockroach': Vijay Mallya cries 'injustice' over bank dues
Article Text:
Vijay Mallya was declared Fugitive Economic Offenders under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018.

Mallya questions his ‘fugitive’ tag

Mentions Rs 14,131.60 crore recovery

The 'fugitive' tag

NEW DELHI: Vijay Mallya , declared a fugitive by the government, quipped on X about "becoming a cockroach", wondering if he may have a "better life on the cockroach side" as he cried "injustice" over legal action linked to his bank dues.Mallya, who is living in London, made the remarks while responding to the legal proceedings against him and defending his position on the recovery of money owed to banks by his now-defunct Kingfisher Airlines "With all the injustices I have faced and continue to face, I wonder if I should become a cockroach. Maybe a better life on the cockroach side," he wrote on X.He cited an Enforcement Directorate (ED) affidavit that he claimed was filed before the Bombay high court and alleged that the agency had confirmed the recovery of more than Rs 14,000 crore and its transfer to banks."And may I say again, affidavit filed in court by the most feared criminal agency the Enforcement Directorate confirms that they handed over Rs 14,000 plus crores to the Banks in 2021. Forget what I say if you don’t trust me. Focus on what the Enforcement Directorate said," he alleged.Mallya also argued that repayment of bank dues should not depend on his physical presence in India."Thank you all for your mixed replies to my tweets. Love and hate go hand in hand and I respectfully accept that whilst humbly accepting your opinions.But for those who do not understand the difference between permanent residency and citizenship and for those who think that repayments are based on physical presence, please think again," he claimed.A day earlier, he had said he was legally unable to leave the UK, where he claimed to have been a permanent resident since 1992."For all who say I am a bhagoda refusing to come to India, please be aware that I have been a permanent resident of the United Kingdom since 1992 and am currently legally prohibited from leaving this country. All this started with poster boy actions by the Government of India who have been grossly unjust in my case," he said in the post on X.Mallya posted what he described as an extract from an ED affidavit filed before the Bombay high court and pointed to the figure of Rs 14,131.60 crore."Affidavit filed by the ED in the Hon’ble Bombay high court. Para 7 is the decreed debt and Para 17 shows recovered Rs 14,131.60 crore in 2021 !! 5 years on I am still referred to as a fraud who cheated the Banks," he said.He also shared a table that he claimed showed the recovery made in his case and questioned why he continued to be described as a fraudster."To all who believe in fair and proper accounting justice please see the following table. Do I still deserve the way I am berated by the media and referred to as a fraudster at the very outset of a journalist’s script ? Why not start asking when I will get my refund," he said.Mallya was among 15 people declared Fugitive Economic Offenders under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018, according to a statement made by MoS Finance Pankaj Chaudhary in the Lok Sabha in October 2025. The list also included Nirav Modi.In February this year, the Bombay high court criticised Mallya and said he could not seek equitable relief while deliberately avoiding court proceedings. The court gave him a final opportunity to clarify whether he intended to return to India.Mallya's petition challenges the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act and his declaration as a fugitive economic offender.
Article Summary: Vijay Mallya, declared a fugitive by the government, quipped on X about "becoming a cockroach" He wondered if he may have a "better life on the cockroach side" as he cried "injustice" over legal action linked to his bank dues. He made the remarks while responding to the legal proceedings against him and defending his position on the recovery of money owed to banks.

NEW DELHI: India’s push for agreement at the BRICS summit beginning Sept 12 faces divisions among its members over the West Asia conflict.Russian officials, speaking to their country’s media, have acknowledged difficult negotiations, while Brazilian reporting has raised doubts about a strong final declaration. Yet Chinese commentary has highlighted opportunities for India’s presidency, including closer trade ties. These contrasting accounts suggest that the challenge for New Delhi is to keep economic cooperation moving while finding language that countries with conflicting security interests can accept.The Sept 12–13 summit at Bharat Mandapam will bring these differences into focus. A final declaration records the common positions that participating countries have agreed to support.Russian deputy foreign minister Sergey Ryabkov told TASS that some members were sharply critical of Tehran’s actions, making the Gulf situation Brics’ most pressing political issue. “And as of today, I cannot predict what the outcome will be,” he said about negotiations on the final document.Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov acknowledged that Iran–UAE differences complicated drafting, but expressed confidence that diplomats would find acceptable wording.The disagreement concerns what members want Brics to say about the conflict. Iran’s Mehr agency reported its judiciary chief’s call at a preparatory meeting for condemnation of US–Israeli attacks. UAE agency WAM highlighted Emirati criticism of Iranian attacks on commercial shipping and demands to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.Chinese commentary has focused on India’s economic strengths. A Global Times article carried by People’s Daily praised its strengths in digital techn and medicine, while saying that bridging differences among members would test Indian diplomacy.Another Global Times commentary advocated deeper India–China trade and greater Chinese market access for Indian products. Indian reporting has highlighted New Delhi’s concerns about Chinese restrictions on critical technologies and industrial components.In Brazil, CNN Brasil reported that President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva would prioritise poll campaigning and send foreign minister Mauro Vieira. South Africa’s Business Day questioned whether expansion had weakened Brics’ unity, while broadcaster SABC highlighted Pretoria’s push for trade, industrialisation and African infra investment.For India, success would mean reaching useful agreements on specific issues while negotiating a common political message among partners whose interests do not always coincide.
Article Summary: India’s push for agreement at the BRICS summit beginning Sept 12 faces divisions among its members over the West Asia conflict. Yet Chinese commentary has highlighted opportunities for India's presidency, including closer trade ties.

SRINAGAR: J&K chief secretary Atal Dulloo Wednesday rolled out a three-year scheme to rehabilitate drug addicts under treatment at govt-run or aided de-addiction centres and institutions, prevent relapse, and aid their reintegration into society.The scheme will initially be introduced in the districts of Jammu, Srinagar, Kathua and Budgam and later extended to others, officials said.Under the scheme, a structured rehabilitation cycle will be established for drug abusers to ensure a seamless transition from “detoxification to socio-economic stabilisation” to reduce relapse rates and prevent premature exit from treatment, Dulloo said.The first six months will cover intake, assessment, treatment, stabilisation and rehabilitation planning under Phase I. The rural development and Panchayati Raj department will support community participation, family engagement, livelihood inclusion, social support networks and local-level rehabilitation and reintegration initiatives. The social welfare department will serve as the nodal department for implementation of the policy, officials said.On April 11, 2026, J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha launched a 100-day anti-drug campaign under the “Nasha Mukt Abhiyaan”, which involved large-scale awareness programmes by the civil administration and police, destruction of poppy cultivation, random urine testing of drivers and intensified crackdowns on drug networks.Over 32,500 drug abuse cases have been registered across J&K since 2022, with the highest number of patients reported from Srinagar and Jammu districts, govt data revealed. Article Title: Can husband be tried for marital rape if law says not offence: Supreme Court
Article Text:
Centre should go back to drawing board if law has a problem, says SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Citing Article 20(1) of the Constitution which shields persons from prosecution for an act which is not an offence under existing penal laws, the Supreme Court on Wednesday asked whether a husband can be prosecuted for marital rape when the law categorically states that it is not an offence, even as it agreed with the Centre that the matter should be left for Parliament’s consideration.Article 20(1) provides that “no person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of law in force at that time…” Section 375(2) of IPC said “sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his wife, the wife not being under 15 years, is not rape” (wife’s age was raised to 18 by SC in 2017), with the provision replicated in Sect 63(2) of BNS.With a bunch of petitions challenging the constitutional validity of this exception to rape, a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the matter posed foundational questions, especially citing the case in which a husband has challenged a Karnataka high court decision to permit his prosecution for marital rape.The hearing saw Solicitor General Tushar Mehta arguing that the issue, given its complexity, be left for the Parliament to consider.It will be absurd for courts to take upon themselves the task of determining the nature of sex — natural or unnatural — when it is best left to people, their representatives and legislature, SG Tushar Mehta said.The bench agreed. “It should always come from Parliament. If the govt feels there is a problem with the law, then it should go back to the drawing board and recast the law with approval of Parliament,” it said.During the last hearing, SC had wondered whether the court can rewrite penal laws to create a new offence.Senior advocate Karuna Nundy said that no new offence needs to be created as the offence of rape is already defined and the only question is whether it is constitutionally justified to grant immunity from it to a class of persons (husbands).
Article Summary: Supreme Court asked whether a husband can be prosecuted for marital rape when the law categorically states that it is not an offence. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta argued that the issue, given its complexity, be left for the Parliament to consider.

Article Title: Indians trust the classroom, see better opportunities abroad: Global survey
Article Text:
File Image

Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani.

for Viksit Bharat@2047

On use of AI

Karmabhoomi

janmabhoomi

Not because the Ipsos Education Monitor survey mirrors the plot of the Shah Rukh Khan-Juhi Chawla film, but because the title neatly captures the contradiction in its India findings. Indians may believe better opportunities for growth and prosperity lie offshore, yet they remain remarkably bullish about their education system, their degrees and, above all, the future of their youth.More than half of Indian respondents rate the country’s education system as good. Three-fourths believe youth will have a better life than their parents. Nearly two-thirds think even young people from lesser privileged backgrounds have a bright future. And Indians remain strikingly convinced that a university degree still has value. However, ironically, 76% of Indian respondents say young people would have better opportunities by moving abroad.For some parameters, TOI looked at the subset of India’s position among the 16 individual G20 member countries included in the 31-country Ipsos survey. China, Russia and Saudi Arabia were not surveyed. The survey covered 23,537 online adults across the 31 countries between June and July 2026, with about 1,000 respondents in India.Ipsos in its methodology has cautioned that its India sample is more urban, educated and/or affluent than the general population and should be interpreted as reflecting the views of the country’s more “connected” segment.The 31-country average is an unweighted average of country results; it is not adjusted for the population size of each country.The first question was straightforward. How do people rate the overall quality of their country’s education system? In India, 51% called it good. Among the G20 countries covered by the survey, only Australia was higher, at 53%. The 31-country average was 33%. But that 51% is a number in retreat. India was at 65% in 2025, 69% in 2024 and 55% in 2023. The 14-point fall from 2025 is the steepest year-on-year decline among countries with comparable 2025 data.The contrast with several richer economies is sharp. Britain was at 43%, the US and Brazil at 32%, Italy at 29%, Japan at 24%, while France and Germany were both at 17%. That does not mean India has a better-performing education system than advanced economies. This is a matter of perception. And on that measure, Indians appear unusually confident. Just less than before.The gap becomes even more striking when the question shifts from institutions to the people coming out of them. Asked whether young people in their country have a bright future, 72% of Indian respondents agreed. That was not merely the highest figure among the G20 countries covered. It was the highest among all 31 countries surveyed. The 31-country average was 45%.Within the surveyed G20 set, Australia and South Africa were next at 54%, followed by Mexico at 52% and Canada at 50%. France was at 22%. It is perhaps one of the strongest votes of confidence in the survey. Indians appear to have placed enormous hope in their youth to put the country on the right track and take it forward.One of the hallmarks of an aspirational society like India is the belief in accumulating wealth and opportunity across generations. People believe that the hard work of one generation will make the lives of those that follow smoother. That belief gets backed in this survey. Three-fourths of Indian respondents, 75%, believe young people today will have a better life than their parents. The 31-country average is 48%.Indians are also optimistic about people escaping the poverty trap. 64% believe young people from poorer backgrounds have a bright future, compared with a 31-country average of 40%. India is the highest among the G20 countries covered on both measures. And 69% of Indian respondents believe the education system contributes to reducing social inequalities, again the highest among the surveyed G20 countries. That figure is also below earlier readings, 72% in 2024 and 79% in 2023.Together, these numbers suggest that Indian respondents continue to see education as a vehicle for upward social mobility. That belief becomes even clearer when the survey turns to higher education. NITI Aayog ’s recent report also points to the continuing pull of degree programmes, noting that vocational pathways are often not seen as credible, growth-oriented alternatives and that degrees can become the safer choice amid limited counselling, social bias and low trust in existing skill systems. The Ipsos survey, albeit with a more urban and connected Indian sample, points in a similar direction. 75% of Indian respondents say a college or university degree is very important to succeed in life. 78% believe it helps people go further in their careers. And 70% say degrees in their country offer good value for money.On the first measure, India is the highest among the G20 countries surveyed. On both the other measures, it ranks second. The contrast with several advanced economies is large. On whether a degree is good value for money, India’s 70% compares with 38% in the US, 41% in Germany, 30% in Japan and 28% in Britain. Ipsos itself finds a strong positive relationship across countries between believing that a degree helps a career and believing that it offers value for money.Here again, the Ipsos study broadly aligns with a concern flagged in NITI Aayog’s skilling report that education and credentials do not automatically translate into the skills and pathways that the labour market demands. The Ipsos survey shows a deep-seated faith in formal education and yet a growing realisation that job-market demands are at times different from what is being taught in the classroom.Asked whether the school curriculum adequately prepares students for future careers, 67% of Indians agree, the highest share among the G20 countries covered by the survey. Even here, the direction has been downward: 74% agreed in 2024, 72% in 2025 and 67% now.Yet in another question on the greatest challenges facing young people, 36% of Indian respondents select “education and training systems not matching labour market demands”. That too is the highest among the G20 countries in the survey.India again falls on one extreme of a scatter plot for its two seemingly contradictory sets of beliefs. On one hand, 72% say young people have a bright future. On the other hand, 76% say young people would have better opportunities by moving abroad. The 31-country average on that question is 62%.Indonesia and South Africa are even more likely to say opportunities are better overseas, at 87% and 80% respectively. Italy is at 79%. Romania matches India at 76%. But none combines that level of outward-looking aspiration with India’s exceptional optimism about the future of its young.This is perhaps the central finding of the entire report for India. Respondents may be optimistic about India’s young people precisely because they believe those young people possess education and skills that give them more options, including the option of leaving. The optimism may be about the people. The doubt may be about the location of opportunity.The dichotomy in the approach of Indians extends to technology too. 78% support banning social media for children under 14, both inside and outside school. The 31-country average is 73%.Support has climbed 10 points in a year. India was at 68% in 2025 and 73% in 2024.On smartphones, 57% of Indian respondents favour a ban in schools, exactly matching the 31-country average. That is up from 50% last year and 52% in 2024. But attitudes to AI are different.Only 26% of Indian respondents say AI, including ChatGPT, should be banned in schools, compared with 39% across the 31 countries. Indian opinion on AI has moved sharply over the four editions of the survey. 39% wanted AI banned in schools in both 2025 and 2024, compared with just 16% in 2023. The 13-point drop from 2025 to 2026 is the largest year-on-year fall among countries with comparable 2025 data.Britain, the US and Poland moved in the other direction, rising to 52%, 56% and 46%, respectively.To sum up, India’s ‘connected’ population has not lost faith in education. Quite the opposite. It remains unusually convinced that education matters, degrees pay, children can surpass their parents and those from poorer homes can climb. What appears less certain is where that promise will ultimately be realised.andmay finally be different. That is the sobering realisation one can derive from this survey.
Article Summary: More than half of Indian respondents rate the country’s education system as good. Three-fourths believe youth will have a better life than their parents. Nearly two-thirds think even young people from lesser privileged backgrounds have a bright future. Indians remain strikingly convinced that a university degree still has value.

SRINAGAR: National Conference fired a political broadside at ally Congress Wednesday, defending full renditions of Vande Mataram at govt functions in J&K as a “constitutional” duty.Congress objected after all six stanzas of the national song was played at the inauguration of J&K’s first international film festival in Srinagar attended by CM Omar Abdullah and NC president Farooq Abdullah on Sept 7. As at other official functions, Omar stood at attention throughout.J&K Congress president Tariq Hamid Karra said NC and Congress should respect how the song’s place in India’s national life evolved through both the freedom movement and constitutional journey. “National symbols, songs and traditions occupy a special place in the heart of every Indian. Their true strength lies in their ability to bind together a nation as diverse as ours,” he said, calling it a concern that alliance partners had chosen to sing the full version.NC countered, asking Congress to look at CMs of states governed by the party, including Telangana and Karnataka, who have participated in full renditions.NC chief spokesperson Tanvir Sadiq shared on X a video featuring Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar at an event where the unabridged song was sung. He said govt protocol must be separated from party ideology. “NC has a clear stand. When Parliament has adopted it, playing Vande Mataram becomes a statutory obligation and that is what govt did,” Sadiq said.CM Omar later shared Sadiq’s statements on X.A Union home ministry protocol directive in Feb mandated the six-stanza version of the song at all state functions, official events and legislature sessions. In Aug, the President cleared Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, which puts Vande Mataram on a par with the national anthem, making disrespect/disruption a punishable offence. The amended law did not change the stanzas, but people are now obligated to respect Vande Mataram as a constitutional duty.NC spokesperson Imran Nabi Dar said: “This is a constitutional obligation, and every one holding a constitutional office has to accept it, whether it is the CM, an MP or anyone else,” he said, adding the full version is now regularly played at govt functions across J&K.Dar acknowledged the objection among Muslims. “Though religiously it is not acceptable to Muslims, it is a constitutional obligation that has to be fulfilled,” he said.The freedom movement broadly adopted first two stanzas of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay’s 1875 poem, while the full song has six containing religious imagery that has drawn objections from Muslims. Congress general secretary GA Mir said freedom fighters had shaped the version used by the movement with inclusivity in mind.(inputs from PTI)
Article Summary: Congress objected after all six stanzas of the national song was played at the inauguration of J&K’s first international film festival in Srinagar. NC countered, asking Congress to look at CMs of states governed by the party, including Telangana and Karnataka.

Article Title: ‘Wanted to teach him a lesson’: Accused on assault that killed Manipuri musician
Article Text:
Accused wanted to ‘teach him a lesson’, police say

Police examine racial angle, dhaba owner’s role

Singh died hours after assault

Northeast body seeks swift, impartial probe

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Who was Chongtham Vikram Singh?

NEW DELHI: The men accused of killing Manipuri musician Chongtham Vikram Singh in southeast Delhi allegedly wanted to “teach him a lesson” for objecting to noise outside his home, but did not expect the assault to turn fatal, police said on Wednesday.During questioning, the accused allegedly told police that they assaulted the 54-year-old musician with fists and blows after he objected to the commotion outside his residence in Kilokari, according to the police, as cited by news agency PTI.Singh had on some occasions complained to the owner of a nearby dhaba about the noise caused by people gathering there, a senior police officer said. However, police had not received any formal complaint from Singh regarding the noise.The dhaba remained open until around midnight and attracted customers from neighbouring areas as well as students living nearby, police said.Police said they were examining all aspects of the case, including whether there was any racial angle. So far, the investigation has not revealed any instance of a racial slur being used against Singh during the altercation, a police source said.The FIR registered at Sunlight Colony police station on the complaint of Singh's son mentions Section 103(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, pertaining to group murder in circumstances covered by the provision.Police are awaiting the post-mortem report to ascertain the exact nature of the injuries sustained by Singh. Prima facie, he appears to have suffered internal injuries that led to his death.The police are also examining the role of the dhaba owner and its operations. So far, no irregularity in the functioning of the establishment has come to light, sources said. Action would be taken against the owner if anything emerges during the investigation.CCTV footage is being scrutinised and witnesses are being questioned to establish the sequence of events and the circumstances that led to the assault.The incident took place around 11.30 pm on Sunday when Singh went downstairs after hearing a commotion outside his home.According to the complaint, when his son heard his father shouting, he opened the door and saw a group of men kicking and punching him.Singh subsequently returned upstairs but complained of breathlessness. His 20-year-old son Yaiphaba took him to Holy Family Hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries around 6 am the following day, police said.Seven men have been arrested and a juvenile apprehended in connection with the case. The accused have been identified as Bharat Kumar, 19, Pramod, 26, Ramzan Khan, 22, Deepanshu, 21, Mohan Vishwakarma, 32, Vijay, 36, and Mannu, 26.The killing has sparked concern among members of Delhi's northeastern community, with several residents alleging that people from the region face racial slurs and discrimination in the national capital.The North Eastern Students' Organisation (NESO) on Wednesday condemned Singh's killing and demanded a swift and impartial probe.NESO chairman Samuel B Jyrwa said the incident was deeply disturbing and called for all those responsible to be brought to justice.“It is deeply disturbing that a person can lose his life merely for raising an objection to disturbance outside his own home. We demand a transparent and impartial investigation and exemplary punishment for every person found responsible,” Jyrwa said in a statement, as cited by PTI.Jyrwa said the killing could not be viewed in isolation from what he described as continuing harassment, racial discrimination, stereotyping, intimidation and violence faced by people from the Northeast in different parts of mainland India.“For years, Northeastern citizens living, studying and working outside the region have repeatedly reported being subjected to racial slurs, verbal abuse, physical attacks, social discrimination and other forms of humiliation because of their appearance, identity and place of origin,” he alleged.NESO urged authorities to treat the matter with seriousness and urgency and ensure that nobody responsible for the crime evades accountability.“The law must be applied firmly and equally, irrespective of the identity or background of the perpetrators,” Jyrwa said.The organisation also called for stronger preventive measures, effective enforcement of the law, sensitisation of police and public institutions, and mechanisms to ensure the safety and dignity of people from the Northeast.“The loss of Chongtham Vikram Singh is not merely a personal tragedy for his family and loved ones, but a matter of deep concern for the entire Northeastern community,” Jyrwa said.Singh had lived in Kilokari for more than two decades. He was a well-known musician and guitarist, and had been the lead guitarist of the Manipur rock band Phoenix in the early 1980s.He later worked as a music teacher and performer in Delhi.NESO expressed solidarity with Singh's family and the people of Manipur and demanded justice for him and accountability for everyone found responsible for his death.
Article Summary: Chongtham Vikram Singh, 54, died hours after being assaulted outside his home. Seven men have been arrested and a juvenile apprehended in connection with the case. North Eastern Students' Organisation (NESO) condemns Singh's killing and demands a swift and impartial probe.

NEW DELHI: Govt on Wednesday approved eight railway multi-tracking projects worth Rs 20,804 crore as part of a big push for faster movement of passengers and goods across its high-density networks. He added that aerial mapping and artificial intelligence–backed monitoring is helping get the actual status of land parcels. The minister also said that land related pre-investment activities are now being started before project sanction.Vaishnaw said 50% of the Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) for Indian Railways for 2026-27 has been spent till the first week of Sept. The two-day BRICS summit in New Delhi, set to kick-off Saturday, will focus on strengthening cooperation in food and energy security, health, disaster resilience and critical supply chains, as member countries seek to build greater resilience amid a fragmented geopolitical environment.The summit, hosted by India under its 2026 chairship, will also cover trade, investment, connectivity and technology, while leaders are expected to exchange views on major global and regional developments.Under India's resilience pillar, leaders will discuss cooperation in areas including health, agriculture, food and energy security, disaster-risk reduction and critical supply chains. The discussions come against the backdrop of disruptions caused by geopolitical conflicts and growing concerns over the resilience of global supply networks.Strengthening intra-BRICS trade and investment, improving connectivity and expanding cooperation in high technology will also be among the key economic priorities. India has placed these areas at the centre of its broader effort to deepen cooperation among emerging economies.The summit will also focus on strengthening multilateralism and making global governance more inclusive. The first closed-door session on Saturday is titled “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism.”Leaders will exchange views on global and regional developments and discuss areas of mutual interest, according to the Ministry of External Affairs.The main open session on Sunday is titled “Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth.” The summit will culminate with the release of the New Delhi Declaration.2:35 pm: Closed-door session for BRICS member countries on “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism”.4:25 pm: Leaders will tour the Bharat Innovates Exhibition.5:05 pm: Leaders will assemble at Bharat Mandapam for the family photo, followed by a joint tree-planting ceremony.7:30 pm: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will host a gala dinner for the leaders.9:55 am: Leaders from BRICS member countries, partner nations and outreach invitees will begin arriving.10:35 am: Official group photo.10:50 am: Open session on “Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth”.The summit will conclude with the release of the New Delhi Declaration.Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Russian President Vladimir Putin, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto are among the leaders expected to attend the summit, reported PTI.The summit comes against the backdrop of the global economy facing disruptions from the Russia-Ukraine war, the West Asia crisis, including concerns over the Strait of Hormuz, and the trade and tariff policies of the Trump administration.With the grouping operating on consensus, questions also remain over whether members will agree on a joint statement, particularly amid differences between Iran and the UAE over the West Asia crisis.BRICS originally comprised Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. The group expanded in 2024 to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia, while Indonesia joined in 2025.Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam became BRICS partner countries in 2025.The grouping now has 11 member countries, representing around 49.5% of the world's population, 40% of global GDP and 26% of global trade, according to the Indian government.India assumed its fourth BRICS chairship on January 1 this year having previously chaired the grouping in 2012, 2016 and 2021.India's chairship is guided by the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, with a stated focus on a people-centric approach rooted in the principle of “humanity first”.Under India's chairship, more than 350 meetings and high-level engagements have been held across more than 25 cities, covering the grouping's three broad pillars: political and security cooperation, economic and financial cooperation, and cultural and people-to-people exchanges.

Article Title: El Nino puts India on high health-risk radar, says WHO

El Nino puts India on high health-risk radar, says WHO

NEW DELHI: With dengue cases rising in several parts of the country, a WHO assessment has flagged India among nations facing high or very high health risks as a strengthening El Nino event alters weather patterns across South Asia.El Nino is a periodic warming of surface waters in central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean that can disrupt weather patterns around the world, influencing rainfall and temperatures far beyond the Pacific.WHO's Global Public Health Situation Analysis - El Nino 2026, released on Sept 5, has identified India as being at high or very high risk, with most of South Asia expected to experience drier-than-normal conditions and above-normal heat during Aug-Oct.The warning comes at a time when vector-borne diseases are already rising in parts of the country. In Delhi, 90 dengue cases were reported in Aug, the highest monthly tally this year, taking the total to 311 by Aug 29. Malaria cases also rose from 17 in July to 53 in Aug, taking the year's tally to 119, according to Municipal Corporation of Delhi.The agency does not link current dengue or malaria cases directly to El Nino, but calls it a risk modifier, with impacts depending on local weather, vulnerability and health-system capacity.For India, heat is a key concern, with higher temperatures potentially causing heat exhaustion and heatstroke and worsening cardiovascular, respiratory, kidney and metabolic illnesses.Extreme heat may also affect maternal and newborn outcomes. Other concerns include malnutrition, food insecurity and worsening non-communicable diseases. Changes in rainfall and water availability could affect food production, while heavy rain and flooding can increase the risk of leptospirosis, particularly where sanitation and drainage are poor. WHO has also flagged the India-Nepal and India-Bhutan borders, where displacement could increase the risk of cross-border disease transmission.
Article Summary: El Nino is a periodic warming of surface waters in central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean. It can disrupt weather patterns around the world, influencing rainfall and temperatures far beyond the Pacific. Most of South Asia expected to experience drier-than-normal conditions and above-normal heat during Aug-Oct.

Article Title: Pay Rs 15L to 'outstanding' officer shunted out as 'deadwood': Supreme Court
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Taking exception to Centre declaring an "outstanding" Indian Trade Service officer "dead wood" and punishing him with compulsory retirement, Supreme Court Wednesday directed all pecuniary benefits and notional promotions to him be restored and ordered govt to pay him Rs 15 lakh as compensation. S S Das was forced to retire in 2018, five years before his superannuation.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu, which had directed Centre to place dossiers and the annual confidential record of the officer before it, found he was consistently graded as outstanding/very good from 1994 and promoted just months before the punishment. It directed govt to grant Das the honourable farewell he would have been entitled to had he not been forced to retire."The manner of decision-making in course whereof 'OUTSTANDING' gradings are completely ignored, grant of promotion is looked upon as if it were a ministerial exercise, followed by a vague and omnibus finding that it is not desirable in public interest to retain the appellant in service, discloses that the officers entrusted to take a decision were determined to ensure the appellant's ouster at any cost and invented reasons to sustain a pre-decided conclusion," the bench said, calling the exercise "sheer abuse of high offices"."Having promoted the appellant, barely a couple of months later, the superior officers in the department could not have branded him... 'dead wood' to justify weeding him out. The two actions are mutually destructive and cannot co-exist," it said.SC said the action demolished the reputation of an officer which was uncalled for. It directed that Das be called to the office by the director general of foreign trade for a farewell with full honours."It must be remembered by all and sundry that reputation is not built overnight. It is built by years of dedicated and selfless service. It comes at a great cost, often at the cost of family life and personal comfort. Such a reputation earned by sweat and toil over decades can, however, be marred by a single stroke of a pen," the bench said.SC said FR 56(j) - which gives Centre the right to prematurely retire a govt servant - should not be exercised lightly or in a casual manner. "It must be founded on material which is credible, cogent and worthy of being acted up-on, and not on mere suspicion and conjecture," it added.
Article Summary: S S Das was forced to retire in 2018, five years before his superannuation. Supreme Court ordered govt to pay him Rs 15 lakh as compensation. Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu found he was consistently graded as outstanding/very good.

Article Title: Creating a multi-layered security grid in Delhi, one Brics at a time

Creating a multi-layered security grid in Delhi, one Brics at a time

NEW DELHI: When the 'Flying Kremlin' and other ultra-secure aircraft touch down in Delhi this weekend, they won't just bring Russian President Vladimir Putin and other high-profile world leaders to the Brics Summit, they will land with a fully autonomous fortress-on-wheels featuring personal food-testing labs, decoy dignitaries and armoured limousines built to survive landmines and chemical attacks.As Delhi transforms into an impenetrable, multi-layered defensive grid, security personnel are bracing for a high-stakes security operation where AI-aimed snipers scan rooftops, gesture-recognition cameras spot human posture shifts, commandos slither down ropes from hovering helicopters and anti-graffiti strike teams patrol the streets 24/7, guarding against everything from high-tech threats to stealth protest tactics.The capital, sources said, hasn't seen security this tight since the 2023 G20 summit, and preparations this time are even more extensive. Unmanned aerial vehicles have been categorised as one of the most potent threats, and systems that can jam drone signals or shoot them down have been installed at several locations.Every dignitary or their hotel or carcade has been assigned a code name or call sign to ensure they are guided smoothly between locations without any overlap or security glitches.Intelligence inputs have hinted at the possibility of flash protests and spray-painting of inflammatory slogans near the venues, targeting some foreign leaders. Cops have formed anti-graffiti teams for round-the-clock patrolling to thwart any such attempts.President Putin's security grid comprises a sophisticated protective shield managed jointly by Russia's Federal Protective Service (FSO) and Indian counter-terrorism forces. Ground mobility will be centred around his custom-made, heavily armoured Aurus Senat limousine, often referred to as a "rolling bunker". Transported directly from Moscow, the state car is built to withstand chemical attacks, landmines and sniper fire, complete with run-flat tyres and an independent emergency oxygen supply.Up in the air, the Russian leader travels in a specially modified Ilyushin IL-96-300PU aircraft, known as the "Flying Kremlin", which operates alongside decoy jets, advanced missile-defence countermeasures and secure command systems. On the ground, the innermost protective layer comprises elite officers from Russian Presidential Security Service (SBP), supported by advanced FSO teams that sanitise every scheduled and potential itinerary venue. The Russian delegation manages its own strict logistics, travelling with personal chefs, portable testing laboratories for food and drink, and measures to collect biological waste, alongside deploying dummy dignitaries in select hotels to boost operational security.Securing the designated summit hotels in central Delhi, Aerocity and Gurgaon presented one of the most formidable logistical challenges for intelligence and law enforcement agencies. Every hotel is being managed as an independent secure zone under its assigned DCP venue commander, supervised by special commissioner-rank officers overseeing broader zones.Within each hotel, two rooms have been repurposed into operational command posts: a primary security control room linked directly to Delhi Police's central C4i command node and a secondary contingency room dedicated to emergency management.To prevent unauthorised access, advanced AI cameras equipped with posture-detection and intrusion-alert software monitor perimeter walls and hallways, capable of flagging unusual physical movements like crawling or wall-scaling. Hotel staff have undergone rigorous multi-round background checks conducted by special branch and special cell, with movement restricted strictly to assigned floors using specially programmed digital keycards.
Article Summary: The capital hasn't seen security this tight since the 2023 G20 summit. AI-aimed snipers scan rooftops, gesture-recognition cameras spot human posture shifts. Unmanned aerial vehicles have been categorised as one of the most potent threats.
