Article Title: Congress-NC rift over Vande Mataram: The ghost of 1987 and ‘big brother’ complex
Article Text:
The 1987 ghost: Vande Mataram row and why Omar Abdullah won't let Congress call the shots in J&K.

Venugopal called on allies to honour the wisdom of the freedom fighters

One alliance, two political vocabularies

The alliance and an unequal power equation

What Omar Abdullah had said in 2024

Statehood: Common demand & source of friction

The Rajya Sabha dispute

We felt that the best chance of winning that seat was with the Congress, and they felt otherwise. So be it. Omar Abdullah on RS seat deadlock

The ghost of 1987

1987: The alliance that became a warning

2009-14: History managed, but not erased

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The latest Congress-National Conference (NC) clash may have begun with a song, but it is really about something much older: who gets to set the political terms of the alliance in Jammu and Kashmir?CM Omar Abdullah and NC president Farooq Abdullah stood through the full rendition of Vande Mataram on Wednesday at the inaugural International Film Festival in Srinagar. The song was played in its complete six-stanza version, lasting about three minutes and 10 seconds, in line with the Centre's new protocol.This was in sharp contrast with the Congress's stand. Its grand-old party has reaffirmed its 1937 decision to restrict public rendition at party events to the first two stanzas, arguing that the later verses sit uneasily with the pluralist ethos of the freedom movement.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal subsequently said the full version "sits uneasily" with the syncretic and pluralist ethos envisioned by India's freedom fighters and urged allies to stand by the Congress position.The NC was quick to respond, saying the J&K government was only fulfilling its official duty. "After legislative enactment by Parliament, singing Vande Mataram and standing for the song has become a statutory obligation (mandatory legal duty) regardless of the ideological position of any party, group or alliance," said National Conference spokesperson Tanvir Sadiq.The Vande Mataram row is the latest in the list of NC-Congress differences that have surfaced post-election.However, in J&K, the dispute carries an additional historical charge.The NC has spent decades constructing its political identity around a particular proposition: New Delhi can be a partner, but it cannot be the political proprietor of Kashmir's choices.That is where the ghost of 1987 enters.The Vande Mataram dispute has once again exposed an asymmetry that has repeatedly surfaced between the two parties.Congress has to balance its position across India. For Abdullahs' NC, the principal political constituency remains rooted in J&K, where questions of identity, autonomy, federalism and the relationship with New Delhi carry a much more immediate electoral meaning.It is also why the latest row is not an isolated irritant in the alliance.In December 2025, for instance, Omar Abdullah explicitly distanced the NC from Congress's "vote chori" campaign, saying Congress was free to choose its own agenda but that it was not automatically the agenda of the INDIA bloc. With this, Omar tried to assert his party's political autonomy within the alliance.And that has been the recurring pattern.The 2024 assembly election gave the NC-Congress relationship a new lease of life, but it also made the asymmetry between the two parties stark.The alliance crossed the majority mark with 49 seats, with the NC winning 42, Congress six and CPM one. The BJP emerged with 29, PDP three and independents seven.The pre-poll negotiations themselves had not been effortless: the parties agreed that NC would contest 51 seats and Congress 32, while several constituencies remained "friendly contests".The campaign also revealed the limits of joint ownership. Congress and NC leaders did not always campaign together. In Sopore, where the two allies were in a friendly contest, Rahul Gandhi and Omar Abdullah campaigned for their respective candidates separately.During the campaign, Omar Abdullah had publicly noted that Rahul Gandhi should dedicate more campaign time and effort to the Jammu region in addition to Kashmir to maximise electoral impact.Omar himself gave the practical reason for the alliance during the campaign: it was intended to prevent a hung assembly and give voters an alternative.The alliance won the election, and the next question was: what does each side get to claim as its own?The first major post-election rupture came even before the new government had settled in.Omar Abdullah became CM in October 2024, but Congress chose to stay out of his ministry, citing restoration of statehood as its priority. While Congress backed the NC government from outside, its absence highlighted a strategic divide within the alliance. Omar had to engage with Delhi to govern the Union Territory, while Congress sought to pressure the Centre from outside. That difference in approach has repeatedly resurfaced.In July 2025, Congress announced protests in Jammu, Srinagar and Delhi and Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge wrote to PM Narendra Modi seeking legislation to restore J&K's statehood. The NC leadership was irritated because the announcement had not been coordinated with the ruling party. Some NC leaders described Congress's campaign as counterproductive and even as "sabotage" of the government's own efforts.Omar's objection was that Congress had launched the campaign without informing or consulting the NC, leaving its alliance partner caught off guard.The difference is clearer on Article 370 . The NC's 2024 manifesto explicitly called for the restoration of Articles 370 and 35A and reversal of the changes made after August 2019. Congress has similarly opposed the 2019 constitutional changes, but in its recent campaigns placed greater emphasis on the restoration of statehood.Omar reiterated in the J&K assembly in February that his government remained committed to restoring special status, even as statehood remained an immediate demand. By July 2026, he was also linking the restoration of statehood to any future discussion on J&K's earlier constitutional position.This has given the two parties different political priorities.In October 2025, the disagreement moved from ideology to seats. J&K was electing four Rajya Sabha members. The NC, which had emerged as the dominant party in the assembly, initially discussed leaving one seat for Congress.Talks failed.The NC eventually fielded candidates for all four seats after Congress decided not to contest the fourth seat it had been offered, arguing that it was not among the "safe seats" it had sought.Omar's response was strikingly matter-of-fact: "So be it."The NC-Congress disagreement ultimately cost the alliance a clean sweep, with the BJP winning the fourth seat Congress had declined to contest.To understand why the NC may be particularly sensitive to questions of control, one has to go back not merely to 1987 but to 1984.Farooq Abdullah's government was dismissed on July 2, 1984, after 12 NC legislators defected. Ghulam Mohammad Shah, Farooq's brother-in-law and leader of the defecting group, formed the government with Congress support. Contemporary accounts described the episode as a central-government intervention in Kashmir politics; Farooq called the dismissal unconstitutional.For the NC, this was not an abstract constitutional episode. It was a direct lesson in the vulnerability of a regional government to New Delhi's political machinery.Then came 1986.Rajiv Gandhi and Farooq Abdullah reached an agreement that brought the two parties together electorally. A Human Rights Watch report noted that the accord deepened a sense of betrayal among many Kashmiris, who saw Farooq Abdullah compromising with the same Congress party that had pushed him out of office two years earlier.The NC-Congress alliance won 66 of J&K's 76 assembly seats in 1987. But the result was overshadowed by the emergence of the Muslim United Front as an opposition platform, arrests of its candidates and workers, and widespread allegations of electoral rigging. Human Rights Watch later described the election as a turning point that contributed to widespread disillusionment with electoral politics.The significance of 1987 for the NC, therefore, is about the political memory it created. A generation of Kashmiri activists came to believe that the democratic route had been closed to them, a perception that became part of the backdrop to the insurgency that followed.The episode also left an enduring paradox. Congress was simultaneously the NC's electoral partner and a major force at the Centre. That history helps explain the NC's instinct to work with Congress while resisting any perception that Delhi is dictating its regional agenda.That distrust predates the 1980s. In 1953, Sheikh Abdullah was dismissed and arrested after his relationship with the Union government deteriorated. The circumstances were very different, but the political memory was similar: central intervention could reshape J&K's politics. For the NC, unlike many other regional parties, Congress's centralising past is therefore not distant history but part of its own political inheritance.The two parties showed they could overcome that history after the 2008 assembly election. The NC won 28 seats and Congress 17, and the parties formed a coalition government with Omar Abdullah as CM in 2009.But the partnership remained contested. Differences over AFSPA, administrative issues and governance repeatedly surfaced. In 2011, Congress called for consensus on AFSPA while Omar maintained that the state government was an important stakeholder.By 2014, the alliance had run its course and Congress chose to contest the assembly election separately. NC leaders argued that the association with a centrist national party had diluted the party's pro-Valley credentials, with one senior NC leader calling Congress a "very bad alliance partner".The 1987 ghost & real test of allianceWhile 1987 may still shape the NC's political instincts, it would be too simplistic to link every present-day disagreement to that history. The political and constitutional context has changed; however, the experience remains part of the backdrop to the relationship.The lesson for the NC, as we saw in the last election, has not been to avoid Congress, but to work with it where interests converge while retaining its own political space.The Vande Mataram dispute, therefore, is less significant in itself than what it reveals about continuing differences over statehood, Article 370, seat-sharing and the balance between Congress's national strategy and the NC's regional politics.The alliance can survive such differences, but the interesting question now is how durable it will be, which willdepend on how well the two parties manage their competing political priorities.
Article Summary: Congress and National Conference (NC) clash over rendition of Vande Mataram. Row is latest in list of NC-Congress differences that have surfaced post-election. But in J&K, dispute carries an additional historical charge. NC has spent decades constructing political identity around a particular proposition. New Delhi can be a partner, but it cannot be the political proprietor of Kashmir's choices.

Article Title: Cyber fraud worth 5,044 crore prevented: Govt
Article Text: NEW DELHI: India is increasingly stopping cyber fraud before money leaves a victim's account. A telecom-led risk system has helped banks and payment platforms prevent suspected fraudulent transactions worth Rs 5,043.7 crore in 15 months, govt said, marking a shift from tracing stolen money to intercepting payments in real time, reports Aabhas Sharma.The Financial Fraud Risk Indicator (FRI), launched by the department of telecommunications in May 2025, assigns mobile numbers medium, high or very high risk ratings. The alerts are fed directly to banks and UPI platforms, allowing them to warn customers or block risky payments.Experts said the system's biggest achievement was making fraud operations costlier.However, fraudsters could turn to SIMs obtained through fraudulent KYC or virtual numbers. An expert said criminals could also evade mobile-number risk scores by obtaining fresh or "aged" SIM cards.
Article Summary: India is increasingly stopping cyber fraud before money leaves a victim's account. Financial Fraud Risk Indicator (FRI) assigns mobile numbers medium, high or very high risk ratings. alerts are fed directly to banks and UPI platforms, allowing them to warn customers or block risky payments.

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi will host a gala dinner for the leaders participating in the Brics summit on Saturday evening, said govt in an announcement Wednesday. The summit will formally begin earlier in the day with Modi welcoming the leaders of Brics member states at the venue, Bharat Mandapam, and later joining them for a closed session titled Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism.India is hosting the 18th Brics summit on Sept 12-13, exactly 20 years after the grouping that counts 11 major emerging economies as members was formalised. UAE will likely be represented by Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.Bridging bilateral divides over the West Asia situation to secure a unified Brics declaration remains the primary hurdle for India, ahead of the meetings.On Sunday - second day of summit - Modi will welcome leaders of the 10 Brics partner countries, along with other outreach invitees. The leaders will join the final session titled Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth.The summit will see a renewed call by Modi for a reinvigorated, inclusive and effective multilateral order at a time when the world is faced with complex challenges. SC reiterates call to CBSE to exempt Class VI from its 3-language policy

New Delhi:New Delhi: Supreme Court Wednesday reiterated its request to the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) to consider exempting Class VI students from the three-language policy, which mandates them to take up at least two native languages, and said this would give them breathing space this academic session.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana told solicitor general Tushar Mehta that CBSE must examine extending the relaxation given up to Class VII to students of Class VI this year.Mehta said that since it has been observed by SC, he, with additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, would call a meeting of CBSE officials along with other officers concerned this week and take a call on this. "We will appraise the court of the decision taken in the next hearing," he said. SC posted the matter for hearing on Sept 17.When the counsel for petitioners referred to Justice Bagchi's earlier observation on how English should be treated - a native or foreign language - Mehta said govt has some issue with the proposition that English is a native language.Justice Bagchi said, "What is logistically less obstructive is the cutoff year for implementation of the three-language policy.Regarding the status of English, it may require full-fledged debate."SC also issued notice to CBSE on a fresh petition filed by the Forum of Minority Schools. Its counsel, Romy Chacko, told SC that it violated their fundamental rights relating to the protection of minority character of educational institutions, institutional autonomy and foundational identity, which are protected under Article 30(1) of Constitution.
Article Summary: SC reiterates call to CBSE to exempt Class VI from its 3-language policy. Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana told solicitor general Tushar Mehta that CBSE must examine extending the relaxation given up to Class VII to students of Class VI. SC posted the matter for hearing on Sept 17.

Article Title: Goods train derails in J&K’s Kathua, no injury or damages
Article Text:
Kathua, J&K (ANI photo)

JAMMU: A goods train derailed at Chann Aroria railway station in J&K’s Kathua district on Wednesday morning. Officials said no one was hurt and no damage was incurred in the incident.The derailment occurred around 9.30am when the goods train was heading back after unloading cement, and one of its coaches went off the track in the station’s yard, officials said. A technical team from Kathua rushed to the spot and brought the derailed coach back on track after two hours of efforts.Earlier on July 10, two bogies of a goods train moving from Jammu to Punjab derailed near Lakhanpur in Kathua after debris fell on the tracks following a rain-triggered landslide.
Article Summary: A goods train derailed at Chann Aroria railway station in J&K’s Kathua district on Wednesday morning. Officials said no one was hurt and no damage was incurred in the incident. The derailment occurred around 9.30am when the goods train was heading back after unloading cement.

SRINAGAR: Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance, the two organisations negotiating with the Union govt for administrative autonomy to Ladakh under the Sixth Schedule, claimed a breakthrough Wednesday in talks with the MHA’s subcommittee in Delhi on legislative powers over land, culture and language, forests and natural resources.In a joint statement, the groups said the meeting furthered the “in-principle understanding” reached during talks on May 22 and July 3 on Ladakh’s demands, including constitutional safeguards through special provisions under Article 371.They said MHA stopped short of guaranteeing powers across the board under Lists II and III of the Seventh Schedule, including law and order.MHA assured compensation to the families of those killed and the protesters injured in the Sept 24, 2025, violence in Leh, the groups claimed. The Union govt also agreed to withdraw cases against 24 people and review those against another 34 on a case-to-case basis. Cases against 25 people have already been withdrawn.Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra wrote on X about the “general air of positivity” at the Delhi meeting without elaborating beyond the agenda. “The broad contours of a sui generis model of governance under Article 371 were discussed. Deepening democracy is the goal,” he said.Another round of talks is scheduled for the first week of Oct.The groups said they were concerned over the formation of new districts, the creation of hill councils for each and what they called “major irreversible changes being done before an elected body at the Union Territory”.Making such changes before the UT body can legislate, they said, “would essentially deprive the people of Ladakh an opportunity to democratically decide on the structure of administration in Ladakh”.Ladakhi representatives have been in talks with MHA since 2023 for safeguards covering land, jobs, culture and environment. MHA set up the committee on Jan 2, 2023, but the process stalled after four people were killed and over 80 injured in alleged police firing on protesters demanding statehood in Leh in Sept last year.Activist Sonam Wangchuk , a LAB member, was accused of inciting the protesters, arrested and charged under the NSA. The Centre revoked his detention last March and he returned to the negotiating table in May.
Article Summary: Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance claim a breakthrough in talks with the MHA’s subcommittee in Delhi. The groups said the meeting furthered the “in- principle understanding’ reached during talks on May 22 and July 3. Article Title: Raghav Chadha’s Delhi voter registration approved after due process: Poll body
Article Text:
Delhi poll body said Raghav Chadha’s voter registration in Rajinder Nagar was approved after the mandatory seven-day notice period, while AAP alleged irregularities

NEW DELHI: The Delhi poll body on Wednesday said BJP Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha’s application to be added to the Delhi voter list was approved after due procedure, days after the AAP questioned his inclusion."As per record available, Raghav Chadha, MP (Rajya Sabha) applied for inclusion of his name in Form 6 in AC-39 (Rajinder Nagar) on August 26," news agency PTI quoted Delhi chief electoral officer as saying."The Form was approved by the Electoral Registration Officer of the AC-39 (Rajinder Nagar) after completion of mandatory notice period of 07 days," it added.The application, numbered U05039D6N2608261200000, was processed under the Election Commission’s prescribed procedure.The AAP, however, rejected the explanation and alleged that Chadha’s name was added to the electoral roll "through the back door". The party also questioned whether political pressure was involved.AAP national media-in-charge Anurag Dhanda demanded that Chadha’s Form 6 be made public and said citizens should be allowed to raise objections against it as they can for any ordinary voter.Dhanda claimed that Chadha’s name did not appear in any Form 6 received in Rajinder Nagar between September 1 and 7.He also questioned how Chadha’s name became the 747th entry when the draft roll had 746 voters and the final roll was yet to be published.The CEO office said eligible persons whose names are not on the electoral roll can seek inclusion by submitting Form 6 with the required documents.It also referred to the Election Commission’s May 14 guidelines on the Special Intensive Revision, which state that additions made during the SIR period would receive serial numbers continuing from the last entry in the draft electoral roll.
Article Summary: Delhi poll body said Raghav Chadha’s voter registration in Rajinder Nagar was approved after the mandatory seven-day notice period. Article Title: Beyond E20? Only flex-fuel vehicles may have the option, indicates adviser
Article Text:
India’s ethanol production capacity has surpassed the requirements for blending, prompting the government to explore additional uses for the surplus.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indicating that govt is unlikely to increase ethanol blending in petrol beyond the current 20% (E20) for existing vehicles, adviser to PM Tarun Kapoor said Wednesday that allowing higher ethanol blending will have to be an option with flex-fuel vehicles.Addressing an event of sugar industry body Isma virtually, Kapoor said E20 has been very successful. “Now, our focus is on going into flex-fuel vehicles and allowing blending at a percentage which will be higher than E20, and definitely it will have to be an option for flex-fuel vehicles,” he added.He noted that several vehicle manufacturers have announced plans to roll out flex-fuel vehicles. These vehicles can run on petrol with higher ethanol blending of up to 85% and even 100% in some cases. Kapoor said there is a possibility of more such vehicles hitting the road while mentioning some petrol pumps are already making higher blends available and that this needs expansion.“But it has to go hand-in-hand with the availability of flex-fuel vehicles,” the top bureaucrat said.Dismissing criticisms against ethanol blending in petrol, Kapoor said it may be due to “misinformation or certain other motivated reasons”.He said a lot of studies and experiments have shown that E20 is good and works very well. Kapoor said there may be “a little bit of fuel efficiency”, but the decline gets compensated with higher octane. He said the issues which are being faced are generally due to “other reasons, not due to this blending”.Kapoor also said if India can also get some product which can be used in diesel, then it will be great considering that in a refinery, a large percentage of the product is diesel.“So we can’t have petrol demand going down, whereas diesel demand is going up. So, we would like to balance that; we need something to add to diesel also. And if experiments are going on on isobutanol, if that succeeds, then that would open another area where biofuels can be required in large quantities, and then that would be great for us,” he added.
Article Summary: India’s ethanol production capacity has surpassed the requirements for blending, prompting the government to explore additional uses for the surplus. Adviser to PM Tarun Kapoor said allowing higher ethanol blending will have to be an option with flex-fuel vehicles.

Article Title: ‘Pilot is a good leader’: Channi backs new Punjab Congress in-charge, says appointment brings ‘new hope’
Article Text:

Congress looks to restart Punjab outreach

NEW DELHI: Former Punjab chief minister and Congress leader Charanjit Singh Channi on Wednesday welcomed Sachin Pilot ’s appointment as the party’s general secretary in-charge of poll-bound Punjab, saying it had brought “new hope” among Congress workers in the state.Channi described Pilot as a “good leader” and said his appointment would benefit the party ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections.“The people of Punjab like Pilot, who comes from the neighbouring state. With his arrival (appointment as in-charge of Punjab), a new hope has arisen among Congress workers in Punjab and it will benefit us. A good leadership has come,” Channi told reporters in Delhi.Channi, Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa and Gurdaspur MLA Barindermeet Singh Pahra met Pilot in Delhi after he was given charge of Punjab.Channi expressed confidence that the Congress would form the next government in Punjab after the 2027 Assembly polls, which are due early next year.Asked whether Congress leaders would come together on one platform, Channi said the decisions being taken by the party leadership were creating a good atmosphere in favour of the Congress in Punjab.“Pilot is a good leader and he is capable of taking all of us along,” he said.The meeting came amid alleged factionalism within the Punjab Congress over the state leadership.When asked about the demand for changing Punjab Congress president Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, Randhawa rejected the suggestion that he or Channi had sought his removal.“When did we tell you that the PPCC president be changed? Did anyone ask about it? Do not say such a thing. Have Channi Saab or I or any leader asked about changing the PPCC,” said Randhawa, the former Punjab deputy chief minister and Gurdaspur MP.Channi also said the decision on the state Congress president was entirely with the party high command.“Who is to be made the president or in-charge, who is to be changed or who is not be changed, it is not in our hands. It is the decision of the party high command. What it decides, we go by it,” he said.The Congress on Saturday carried out a major organisational reshuffle and appointed Pilot as general secretary in-charge of Punjab, replacing Bhupesh Baghel.Pilot had until then been in charge of Chhattisgarh, where Baghel is a key leader and former chief minister. Baghel has now been assigned Assam, replacing Jitendra Singh.The differences within the Punjab Congress intensified after the party leadership on July 1 decided to retain Warring as the state unit chief and appoint Channi as chairperson of its campaign committee.A section of Congress leaders led by Channi opposed the decision to retain Warring and sought his removal.Channi’s supporters had openly demanded Warring’s removal as Punjab Congress chief and sought to have the Jalandhar MP declared the party’s chief ministerial face for the 2027 Assembly elections.Baghel’s recent visits to Punjab did not end the factionalism, while Channi’s supporters also accused him of “favouring” Warring.Warring had welcomed Pilot’s appointment and said there was no resentment among party leaders. He had expressed confidence that all leaders would come together to fight the elections.“There is no resentment. I think you will see that in the coming time, there may be some minor differences, but all of us, all the leaders, will come together on one platform and fight,” Warring had said.Warring had also described Pilot as a “national leader” and a “very dear colleague”, saying he was an “exceptionally hardworking and dynamic leader”.Senior Congress leader Raj Kumar Verka had also welcomed Pilot’s appointment, saying it would benefit the party and that Pilot’s experience and understanding of Punjab would help resolve the “minor mutual issues” within the state unit.The Congress is now looking to revive its organisational and electoral activities in Punjab ahead of the 2027 polls.The party is planning a statewide yatra in Punjab featuring Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, which could be held towards the end of September or in early October, subject to the festival calendar.The party had announced its election-related committees on July 1, but their functioning was affected by the subsequent differences within the state unit.With Pilot replacing Baghel as the Punjab in-charge, Congress leaders have publicly welcomed the change as the party prepares for the next Assembly election.
Article Summary: Former Punjab chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi welcomed Sachin Pilot ’s appointment as the party’s general secretary in-charge of poll-bound Punjab. Channi described Pilot as a ‘good leader’ and said his appointment would benefit the party ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections.

Article Title: Baba Neem Karoli’s granddaughters claim their ancestral home illegally occupied by trust

NEW DELHI: A dispute has erupted over the ancestral home of Hindu saint Baba Neem Karoli Maharaj in Uttar Pradesh, with his six granddaughters alleging that the property is being illegally occupied and controlled by a trust headed by their aunt, PTI reported.Following the complaint, Firozabad District Magistrate Santosh Kumar Sharma has constituted a three-member committee to investigate the ownership and management of the property, according to PTI.The committee is headed by additional district magistrate (Judicial) Arvind Kumar Dwivedi and includes Tundla Sub-Divisional Magistrate Divya Singh and District Tourism Officer Vishal Srivastava.The dispute concerns house number 154 and adjoining structures in Akbarpur village under Tundla tehsil, the birthplace of Baba Neem Karoli, whose original name was Lakshmi Narayan Sharma, according to PTI.The property, which is being developed as a tourist attraction by the Uttar Pradesh tourism department, includes the saint's meditation room, dining area, guest quarters and bedroom.The ancestral residence is a duplex built on a plot measuring around 4,000 square feet and is currently managed by the Shri Neem Karoli Maharaj Trust, headed by the saint's daughter Girija Devi Bhatele. His late wife Rambeti was its former president.According to family sources cited by PTI, the dispute came to the fore during a family event on August 24, when the six daughters of the saint's late son Dharm Narayan Sharma were allegedly denied accommodation in rooms at the ancestral property.Following the incident, the six granddaughters, Sunita Sharma, Archana Sharma, Vandana Sharma, Bhavna Rawat, Ritu Tiwari and Richa Rawat, submitted a representation to the District Magistrate seeking that the ancestral residence be freed from the Trust's control, PTI reported.Manoj Rawat, husband of Bhavna Rawat, confirmed to PTI that relevant property documents had been submitted to the inquiry committee after it sought them.However, Dhananjay Sharma, son of the saint's other late son Anek Singh Sharma, rejected the allegations and said that the property had been handed over to the Trust in accordance with Baba Neem Karoli's wishes.He expressed concern over the public nature of the dispute and appealed to family members to resolve the matter amicably.Trust secretary Sanjay Gupta also denied allegations of illegal occupation and rejected claims of an internal dispute within the Trust. He said he had been appointed by Dharm Narayan Sharma and continued to serve the institution.Gupta told PTI that the Trust had not received any official notice from the district administration so far.The dispute comes amid renewed public interest in Baba Neem Karoli's life and legacy following the release of Hanuman Ansh, a devotional biographical film based on the saint's life.Released on August 7, 2026, the low-budget film starring Shobhinaww Satyaa became a sleeper hit following strong word-of-mouth publicity. It reportedly collected more than Rs 150 crore worldwide within a month, bringing renewed attention to the saint's life and his birthplace, PTI reported.
Article Summary: dispute erupts over ancestral home of Hindu saint Baba Neem Karoli Maharaj. Six granddaughters allege property is being illegally occupied and controlled by a trust headed by their aunt. Firozabad District Magistrate has constituted a three-member committee to investigate the ownership and management of the property.

Article Title: India considers it a responsibility, not a favour, to provide aid to Sri Lanka as first responder: Rajnath to president Dissanayake

Defence minister Rajnath conveyed greetings on behalf of PM Modi and underlined that the citizens of the two countries share deep friendship based on strong historical and civilisational links and people-to-people exchanges. He emphasised that as a closest friend and neighbour of Sri Lanka, “India considered it not a favour, but a responsibility to provide assistance as the first responder and would continue to do so in the future as well”.Sri Lankan president Dissanayake said his country would never allow its territory to be used for activities inimical to India’s security interests. He also expressed his gratitude for the relief assistance provided by India as part of Op Sagar Bandhu during Cyclone Ditwah and the comprehensive rehabilitation package extended by New.Both leaders virtually inaugurated three Bailey bridges constructed by the Indian defence forces. The two sides also exchanged MoUs on upgradation of L70 guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force, and cooperation between NCC and National Defence Colleges of both the countries.Rajnath also met Sri Lankan PM Harini Amarasuriya. “We exchanged views on a range of issues related to development cooperation, education and close cultural and civilisational ties,” he posted on X.He underlined that as “sister democracies with shared heritage”, India and Sri Lanka should continue working towards a shared developmental vision for the peace and prosperity of the region. Rajnath also highlighted Sri Lanka's importance in India's Vision MAHASAGAR, saying the island nation holds a special place in the policy and would continue to do so in the future.Rajnath called for enhanced cooperation between India and Sri Lanka to shape a favourable and secure maritime environment and tackle emerging maritime challenges before they evolve into serious threats to developmental interests and brighter future. “Secure sea lanes, freedom of navigation, respect for international law and unhindered maritime trade are pivotal for collective security & prosperity of the Indian Ocean Region (IOR),” the defence minister said while addressing a gathering comprising Sri Lankan deputy minister of defence Aruna Jayasekara, commanders of the Sri Lankan three services.Rajnath said India and Sri Lanka are bound by the shared ocean, and maritime security is not a matter of abstract theory but a reality that shapes their trade, security and destinies. “Both nations are central to any strategic discourse on maritime security in the region. Strong India-Sri Lanka maritime cooperation will be mutually beneficial and vital for collective growth and security,” he said.Referring to the challenges faced by our fishermen, the defence minister underscored that the issue needs to be addressed together. He observed that maritime cooperation should extend beyond the security framework to also cover areas like aquaculture, marine biotechnology, ocean science, protection and preservation of maritime environment and maritime tourism.He also suggested that the two countries can explore the establishment of a joint Maritime Humanitarian Assistance & Disaster Relief (HADR) system involving relevant agencies for a coordinated and rapid response to natural calamities and man-made disasters.Rajnath also laid a wreath at the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) Memorial in Battaramulla and paid homage to the bravehearts who made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty.
Article Summary: Sri Lankan president Dissanayake said his country would never allow its territory to be used for activities inimical to India’s security interests. He expressed his gratitude for the relief assistance provided by India as part of Op Sagar Bandhu during Cyclone Ditwah.

Article Title: India launches ORV Sagar Manthan, boosting ocean research fleet
Article Text:
ORV Sagar Manthan, built under the Deep Ocean Mission at a cost of around Rs 840 crore, will boost India’s ocean research capabilities.

NEW DELHI: The Government on Wednesday launched state-of-the-art ocean research vessel ORV Sagar Manthan at Rishi Bankim Shipyard in Kolkata, boosting India’s efforts towards self-reliance in oceanographic science and maritime technology.Constructed under Vertical-4 (Deep Ocean Survey and Exploration) of the government’s flagship Deep Ocean Mission (DOM) at a cost of around Rs 840 crore, the vessel is an all-weather, multidisciplinary platform. It is engineered to operate in extreme oceanic environments, including the Southern Ocean, with a projected service life of 30 years.The ORV Sagar Manthan, designed, engineered and constructed by defence public sector undertaking Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE), will gradually replace the iconic 43-year-old ORV Sagar Kanya, procured from Germany in 1983.“Today, the world knows very little about our oceans, yet they provide vital inputs about melting polar glaciers, maritime impact, and climate dynamics. Solid data collected by vessels like ORV Sagar Manthan will allow India to lead the global path in disaster prevention, take corrective environmental measures, and play a pivotal role in global ocean geopolitics,” said Union minister of earth sciences Jitendra Singh, who virtually joined the launch event.ORV Sagar Manthan will support multidisciplinary exploration along Indian Ocean mid-oceanic ridges to identify multi-metal hydrothermal sulphide mineralisation, establish environmental baselines and collect upper-air data. It integrates dynamic positioning, multibeam bathymetry, multichannel seismic systems, sub-bottom profiling, weather radar, drop keels and deployment facilities for remotely operated and autonomous underwater vehicles.
Article Summary: The vessel is an all-weather, multidisciplinary platform. It is engineered to operate in extreme oceanic environments, including the Southern Ocean. It will gradually replace the iconic 43-year-old ORV Sagar Kanya, procured from Germany in 1983.

Article Title: Centre clears separate engineering cadre for Delhi PWD
Article Text:
Centre clears separate engineering cadre for Delhi PWD

NEW DELHI: The Centre has approved the Delhi government's proposal to create a separate engineering cadre for the Public Works Department (PWD), a move expected to give the capital greater control over its engineering workforce and help speed up infrastructure projects.Under the decision, 3,214 sanctioned engineering posts across 36 categories in Delhi PWD will be separated from the Central Public Works Department (CPWD) cadre and brought under an independent Delhi PWD Engineering Cadre.Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta welcomed the approval, describing it as a historic step towards making Delhi a developed, safe and world-class capital.The Delhi government said the separate cadre is intended to address a long-standing administrative issue and make the PWD's engineering system more responsive to the capital's specific requirements. The proposal had earlier been approved by the Delhi Cabinet under Gupta's leadership.The issue has remained pending for nearly 30 years. Until now, Delhi PWD's engineering services were largely dependent on the CPWD cadre, with appointments to its sanctioned posts being made through the Central government's system.According to the Delhi government, this arrangement could sometimes make it difficult to take decisions quickly in line with Delhi's own development and administrative requirements.Gupta said Delhi's infrastructure needs are distinct because of the scale and pace of development in the national capital. The city requires continuous construction and maintenance of roads, bridges, government buildings, offices and other public infrastructure.With the creation of a separate cadre, the Delhi government will have greater control over its engineering workforce. It will be able to manage issues such as filling vacancies, ensuring the availability of engineers, monitoring projects and deploying officials according to the requirements of different works.The government also expects the new arrangement to help build an engineering workforce more familiar with Delhi's local infrastructure challenges and development priorities.The move comes as the government prepares to undertake several major construction and development projects. These include a new secretariat and mini-secretariats in all 11 districts, besides work related to mandis, sports grounds and other public facilities.Roads, bridges and other infrastructure projects will also require sustained engineering support across the capital.The government said the reform is not limited to changing the administrative structure of engineering posts. It is also intended to improve accountability and transparency in the execution of public works.Gupta said that under the earlier system, instances involving deficiencies or irregularities in construction projects could sometimes make it difficult to fix responsibility, particularly when the concerned officer was transferred.A separate Delhi PWD cadre, the government said, would allow the responsibilities of engineering officials and the monitoring of their work to be linked more closely with the Delhi government's administrative system.The Centre's approval now provides the formal basis for Delhi PWD to establish an independent engineering cadre. The government believes the move will make the department more self-reliant and help ensure greater continuity in the planning, execution and supervision of infrastructure projects.For a rapidly developing capital facing growing demands on its roads, public buildings and other infrastructure, the decision marks a significant administrative change that could shape how Delhi's public works are planned and delivered in the years ahead.
Article Summary: The Centre has approved the Delhi government's proposal to create a separate engineering cadre for the Public Works Department. The move is expected to give the capital greater control over its engineering workforce and help speed up infrastructure projects. Until now, Delhi PWD's engineering services were largely dependent on the CPWD cadre.
